clue.text: Obligation to hold record for second-in-command

indicators.note: to hold says the obligation word wraps round the record word

parts.note: an obligation is a duty
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone's duty is to keep the records for the deputy boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' is the containment signal: the obligation wraps the record. An EP is a short vinyl record with a few tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is the person ranked directly below the chief, standing in when needed.

clue.text: Observation pause holds one back

indicators.note: back tells us the built word is read from right to left
holds says the pause word contains the letter for one

parts.note: a lapse is a pause or interval
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Watching something involves a pause that holds someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts I inside LAPSE to make LAIPSE, and 'back' reads that from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying or noticing, the act of watching closely.

clue.text: Grips metal fasteners

explanation.surface: A pair of descriptions of the things that hold metal plates together.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to rivet is to hold attention fast (grips); as a noun, rivets are metal pins joining plates.

clue.text: Total fury under hospital department

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the fury word below the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
ire means fury or anger

explanation.surface: Complete rage breaks out below a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, the same as total as an adjective.

clue.text: Goes by air with ruler covering island sport

parts.note: to jet is to travel by plane, so goes by air is jets

indicators.note: covering says the ruler word wraps round the island letter

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch flies out to an island to enjoy a water sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts I inside KING to make KIING.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetskiing is riding a small motorised water vehicle, a recreational sport.

clue.text: Roomy enough for accountant to get nervous again

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: again suggests the word nervous is made afresh, rearranged into new letters

explanation.surface: A space big enough for a bookkeeper to get jittery once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' is the anagram signal, making the word nervous anew. 'enough for' and 'to get' are link words joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavernous means vast and hollow like a cave, so very spacious.

clue.text: A cereal store returned to Greek citadel

parts.note: a crop is a cereal harvest such as wheat

indicators.note: returned says the store word is turned back, read right to left

parts.note: a silo is a store for grain

explanation.surface: A grain store has been sent back to an ancient Greek fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis is the fortified hilltop citadel of Athens, and the word means any such Greek stronghold.

clue.text: Short girl goes to country with one dog

parts.note: Sal is a shortened form of the girl's name Sally
UK is the United Kingdom
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young woman travels to Britain with her pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender hunting hound bred in the Middle East.

clue.text: Demonstrate point to five in church

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
V is the Roman numeral for five
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A preacher shows the way to five worshippers inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a quality clearly.

clue.text: Skill seen as party piece

indicators.note: piece says the answer is a part taken from inside the word party

explanation.surface: Someone's talent is wheeled out as their party trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party piece' looks like one idiom; 'piece' signals a run of letters inside 'party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean craft or knack, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: Wobbly dessert spilt on Kevin, initially, and Mr Hyde's other half

indicators.note: spilt suggests the dessert has fallen and spread into a new arrangement

parts.note: jelly is a wobbly dessert

indicators.note: initially picks only the opening letter of the name Kevin

explanation.surface: A trembling pudding is knocked over onto Kevin, who has a dark alter ego.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges JELLY with K, the first letter of Kevin, which 'initially' picks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's novella, respectable Dr Jekyll and brutal Mr Hyde are the same man.

clue.text: In gale eventually find shelter

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across a word break

explanation.surface: During a storm you eventually find somewhere protected.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee is the side sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: Understand why pronoun is so long

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see
you is a second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle about why a pronoun makes a sentence long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'why' asks the question the solver answers with 'see you', as in 'I see' plus the pronoun; 'so long' is the farewell, not a length.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are casual farewells said when parting.

clue.text: Good person leaves Steve with her

indicators.note: leaves says the good person departs, taken out of the name Steve

parts.note: ST, for saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A virtuous woman walks out on Steve to be with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in Genesis, so it can stand for a female pronoun.

clue.text: Joins together furniture around end of June

indicators.note: around says the furniture word encloses the letter taken from June

parts.note: units are pieces of fitted furniture, as in kitchen units

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word June

explanation.surface: Flat-pack cabinets are assembled at the end of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts E, the last letter of June, inside UNITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to combine or bring into one.

clue.text: Score heartless try without being irritable

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the trimmed try wraps the score word
heartless removes the middle letter from the word try

parts.note: taken as written
to score is to scratch or etch a mark

explanation.surface: Missing out on scoring a try makes a player grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle letter and 'without' here means outside, round the score word. 'Score' looks like points or twenty; it means scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means bad-tempered and easily annoyed.

clue.text: Globe in hardened water ice

indicators.note: in puts the globe word inside the word for hardened

parts.note: something set has hardened, as jelly sets
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: A round ball frozen inside solid ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal. 'hardened' suggests ice; here it is the word for something that has set firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a frozen dessert of sweetened fruit juice, also called a water ice.

clue.text: Red wine in summer lottery

indicators.note: in says the answer is a run of letters within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bottle of claret offered as a prize in a summer raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Some blamed us, apparently for mythical creature

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that some people seem to blame us for a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for mythical creature' as the definition; 'for' is a link word, so the definition is 'mythical creature'. The run sits across 'blaMED US Apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the snake-haired Gorgon of Greek myth whose gaze turned people to stone.

clue.text: Kick on before spring

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a memo heading
a coil is a spring, as in a coiled spring

explanation.surface: A footballer takes a kick on just before springing forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's kick is the backward jolt when it fires, its recoil.

clue.text: Love the French matador's cry

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A French lover cheers on a bullfighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators at a bullfight shout this Spanish word of approval as the matador makes a pass.

clue.text: Predator organised the run

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A hunting animal has planned its chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the letters of THE RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is any animal or person that pursues prey.

clue.text: Pole leaves enticed, turning to fraud

indicators.note: turning says the remaining letters are twisted round into a new order
leaves says the pole letter goes out of the word enticed

parts.note: N is the North Pole, a magnetic pole

explanation.surface: Someone lured in walks away when the trick turns to swindling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes N out of ENTICED, leaving ETICED, and 'turning' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceit is deliberate trickery or dishonesty.

clue.text: Fleece from older lamb's family

parts.note: a grown-up lamb is a sheep, so this is sheep's
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A wool coat taken from the family of an older lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a sheep's hide with the wool on, a fleece.
